novelty_instruction: Assess the cited span in its source context and known entity candidates. Return only JSON with kind (date or name), novel (boolean), confidence (integer percent), and entity (one supplied candidate id or null). Novel means new information worth retaining, not merely an unfamiliar spelling. Do not invent entity ids. A low score never discards the span.
typing_instruction: Resolve the uncertain cited span using its source context and the novelty reading. Return only JSON with kind (date or name), novel (boolean), confidence (integer percent), and entity (one supplied candidate id or null). Do not invent entity ids. This is a typed classification, not permission to write a belief.
narrative_instruction: Write a concise arc summary from only these child proposals and their ids. Preserve disagreements and uncertainty. Cite the proposal ids. Name each person, place or thing by its name, never by a label such as P1. Do not infer new facts, decide conflicts, copy an earlier summary, or treat a proposal as approved truth.
follower_instruction: You follow one append-only log of source frames. Each frame is labelled F<n> and holds its chunks in order; the frames before the question are what you have already read, and a keyframe stands in for the frames it folds. The last part lists spans, each with its ordinal, frame, chunk, quoted words, cheap reading and entity candidate labels. Return only JSON {"readings": [...]} with exactly one item per listed span: span (its ordinal), kind (date or name), novel (boolean), confidence (integer percent) and entity (one of that span's candidate labels, or null). Novel means new information worth retaining, not merely an unfamiliar spelling. Do not invent labels or ids, and do not skip or repeat a span. A low score never discards the span.
follower_keyframe_instruction: Fold the listed parts, frames labelled F<n> and any earlier keyframe, into one keyframe that is read in their place. Keep every fact, date, name, open question and uncertainty they carry, and cite the frame labels each comes from. Do not infer new facts, decide conflicts, or drop a part. Return only the keyframe text.
audit_window_instruction: The window is a stretch of source text in which the cheap rules flagged no date and no name. List every date mention and every name of a person, organisation or place in the window text. Return only JSON {"discovered": [...]}, each item with source (the window's source label), quote (words copied exactly from the window text, enough that they occur only once in it), kind (date or name) and confidence (integer percent). Return {"discovered": []} when the window holds none; that is a full answer, not a failure. Do not invent labels or ids.
thing_child_instruction: Read every lent input piece. Use only the lent extract and decide ports. Return the engine-issued proposal refs the extract answers gave and the exact coverage and checkpoint refs. Never write vault entities or infer source trust.
